newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals seen opening sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals seen opening sharply higher.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious were called to open sharply higher on Wednesday as the gold-led complex appeared more sure-footed and poised for higher numbers, dealers said.
COMEX August gold was called to open up $2.50 to $3.00 an ounce from Tuesday's close at $319.00, after trading between $322.00 and $317.60 in overnight ACCESS trade.
In London gold was fixed at $319.50 an ounce on Wednesday morning, down 75 cents from Tuesday's afternoon fix. Bullion was quoted at $320.80/$321.30 by dealers.
COMEX September silver was due to open 2.0-3.0 cents up.
COMEX gold stocks on Tuesday fell 32 ounces to 869,659 ounces, while silver stocks rose 395,396 ounces to 180,034,449 ounces.
On ACCESS September silver was last traded at $4.335 an ounce, up 3.8 cents from Tuesday's close at $4.297 an ounce.
NYMEX October platinum and NYMEX September palladium were both seen opening up $1.50 to $2.00 an ounce, after closing at $386.40 and $152.30 an ounce respectively on Tuesday.
U.S. consumer prices for June, forecast to rise 0.2 percent compared with an increase of 0.1 percent in May, are due at 0830 EDT.
May's U.S. business inventories were also due at the same time.
